title: Spring with dry friction

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a spring with dry friction: k/m = 100 s⁻², friction 0.45 m/s²)

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, narration or visual indication of slow motion; animation plays as continuous oscillation

subjects.description: small blue rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical coil spring

observation.what_happens: A blue block hung from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the centre of the frame. It starts from a low stretched position, moves upward as the spring contracts, then continues bouncing vertically as the spring stretches and contracts.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s data shows ~0.6 s period vertical oscillation around ~100 pixels with amplitude decaying from ~85 to ~40 pixels over 2.8 s, classic damped spring in air. Candidates go from ideal textbook harmonic motion to linear viscous damping to linear plus quadratic air drag to test what loss best predicts the held-back decay.

law.title: Spring with dry (Coulomb) friction plus weak viscous damping
law.summary: The block rubs as it moves, so a constant friction force always opposes its velocity and makes the bounce shrink linearly, with only a tiny viscous drag.

critique.finding: The block hangs and bounces with natural wobble {omega} around rest spot {seq}. It loses energy mostly to steady dry rubbing {mu} with only a whisper of viscous drag {gamma}.
critique.headline: Rubbing slows the spring bounce, not air drag
critique.why_it_won: The winner nails the even line-like shrinking of the swings from dry rubbing, while viscous-only damping makes the fade too quick at first and too slow later.

headline: Muse Spark’s laws used air drag. Muse Wonder found the friction is dry.
finding: The block hangs and bounces with natural wobble 9.99989 ± 0.00077 rad/s around rest spot 99.033 ± 0.026 pixel. It loses energy mostly to steady dry rubbing 363.0 ± 5.1 pixel/s² with only a whisper of viscous drag 0.0157 ± 0.0097 1/s.

eyeball.confidence: low - only first frame visible, values are typical-order estimates for a vertical mass-spring demo
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass position follows damped harmonic motion about gravity-spring equilibrium: x'' + gamma x' + omega^2 (x-seq)=0, so x(t)=seq + A exp(-gamma t/2) cos(omega_d t+phi)

wonder.idea: The winner misses even the frames it was fitted to by 14.2 times the measurement noise; some effect is missing.
